note: Per-route performance ceilings for every route the site serves a stranger, all 35 of them. Read docs/PERFORMANCE_BUDGETS.md before changing a number: down is free, up is a decision, and scripts/check-budget-ratchet.mjs refuses an undocumented raise against the base branch. Re-seeded 2026-09-04 from a five-sample sweep on a production build of main at 0eaa7c6f5, under the method block below. The margin is PER METRIC, because the four do not behave alike: bytes and requests take the p75 plus 15%, being identical across every sample of every route; server render takes the p75 plus 50% over a 150 ms floor, because single-digit milliseconds make a percentage meaningless; and LCP takes the WORST sample any sweep has produced plus 25%, because its spread is BETWEEN runs rather than within them and reached 3.17x one route's own p75. Seeding LCP from a single run's p75 would rebuild the gate this programme began by fixing. Every ceiling here is the same or lower than the one before it; nothing was raised, and no route's ceiling sits below a figure we have measured. CI's own sweep is the oracle and the ratchet check banks the slack.

method.resampleWhy: A median of 3 is only a median when the samples agree. On the Avrea runners the 6 September sweep reported LCP spreads of 37 to 51 percent on /today, /discover, /drinks and /crawls, past this method's own 12 percent width, so a route flipped between pass and fail on one commit. A route whose spread passes sampleSpreadWarnPct on any metric is measured twice more and its median is taken over 5 samples. Extra samples are only ever taken where the run said it could not measure, so a quiet route costs nothing and a noisy one is judged on more evidence rather than on less.

network.why: Chrome DevTools' own Fast 4G preset, written out in its own units: 9 Mbit/s down and 1.5 Mbit/s up at 90% of nominal, with a 20 ms base round trip scaled by 3.75. Loopback has no round trip at all, so it cannot see a waterfall, and a waterfall is what the requests ceiling exists to catch. The numbers are here rather than in code because two runs are only comparable when the wire under them was the same.

method.futureDeviceMigration: A later DPR-3 migration is possible, but it must re-seed every ceiling in one commit. playwright.config.ts already has iPhone 14 wiring; the cost is re-measurement, not plumbing.
method.countedUpTo: route interactive: the later of the document's own load event and the first in-page frame on which the route's readiness gate held. A resource counts if it STARTED before that moment, so the post-paint background warmup is excluded by construction rather than by how fast the box is.

routes.why: The landing every shared link and every search result opens.

The front door's one primary action, so it is measured beside the landing that sends people to it. The 2026-09-01 seed sweep measured 1745 KB decoded, of which a single 603 KB chunk was the ElevenLabs conversation SDK, parsed before first paint for a control the reader may never reach and the deployment may not even have switched on. That chunk now loads when the availability probe says voice is on (components/pubpal/PubPalVoiceSession.tsx), so this ceiling ratchets to 1300 KB against an expected ~1142 KB. CI's sweep is the oracle; U8's ratchet check banks whatever slack is left.

The product. Its data loads client side, so the document is a shell and must stay one. This route is why the throttled rig exists: on its first full sweep it asked for 331 requests before it was interactive, against 148 before the map camera work landed. MapLibre reports its own maxBounds as the visible bounds until the camera settles, so a cold open briefly said it was looking at the whole United Kingdom and the shard ring took it literally, fetching all 244 London cells twice. boundsNameNowhere (lib/slimShards.ts) refuses a read from bounds that name no place, and the figure is now 125. The ceiling stays at 160 rather than ratcheting to the median, because the widest sample in that run was 147.

pinReady.note: Cold first visit on phone; pinReadyMs from e2e/mobile-map-chrome-fit.spec.ts on a production build with one Chromium worker and the pin SLA enforced. The target comes DOWN from 4000 to 2500 here. The measured figure is 2713, the median of five runs on the map lane's own box after #1378, so 2500 is a baseline to beat rather than a ceiling that has been met: the gap is 213 ms and it is debt, not a licence to raise the number back. (A single run on this box measured 1822 ms before #1378 landed; five runs after it is the figure to trust.) Local pub pins reveal from their painted source without waiting for remote basemap tiles; the basemap retains its independent recovery lane. The SPEC reads targetMs from here, so there is one owner of the number, and scripts/check-budget-ratchet.mjs refuses a commit that takes it back up. It is enforced only where a real renderer is available (PUBMAX_PIN_SLA_ENFORCE=1): a GPU-less runner measures SwiftShader rather than the map.

routes.why: The morning brief, composed on the server from bundled data. Its server figure is the loosest here because it is the one route that really composes something.
The fastest route we have. It is the shape every other route is held against.
The Out tab shell. Composed from existing what's-on rows; no new API.

The page that states what the figures mean and where they come from, linked from every trust claim on the site. It composes nothing per request, so it is the floor a server-rendered page here should sit on. The 1900 KB ceiling was stale by 800 KB: the 2026-09-01 sweep measured 1081 KB decoded over 24 chunks with no MapLibre, no Convex, no voice SDK and no image cropper in any of them, so there was no accidental import to split, only slack to bank. The REQUEST ceiling is left where it is: a seed run counts requests against its own interactive moment on a different box and network, and this one counted 62 on / where CI is green at 50, so a request figure measured here is not comparable to the sweep's. Decoded bytes are.

The one launch surface whose server render was not a shell: it re-parsed the 6.7 MB price dataset per request until the shared priced-venue index was reused. The ceiling is here so that read cannot come back unnoticed. Its JS ceiling was stale by 850 KB: the 2026-09-01 sweep measured 1092 KB decoded over 25 chunks, the same shared baseline /about carries, with none of the heavy libraries in any of them. Its request ceiling is left alone for the reason /about's is.

The Agent Night Board. It is unlinked and noindex, so nobody arrives here by browsing, but it is a route a judge and an agent both open and it must not become the place heavy work hides. Seeded from the 2026-09-03 sweep on this branch: 13 ms server render, 863 KB decoded, 37 requests, 184 ms LCP. The board fetches nothing on mount, so those figures are the shell; every read here answers a person or agent action afterwards. Ceilings are set in family with /about and /pubs, which measure about 830 KB against 1200 KB, rather than at the measured figure, because a request count measured on one box is not comparable to CI's. CI is the oracle: take these DOWN at the next sweep, never up.
The instant answer: the cheapest good pints within a walk. It is the one arrival that is measured in the UX lane report and budgeted nowhere, so nothing could regress it.
The door. Every account this product ever gets comes through it, and it is the one surface where a slow paint costs a person rather than a page view.
The live alias of /login, budgeted separately because an alias that quietly diverges from what it aliases is worse than two pages.
Describe-first: the composer a night is actually built in.
Where the front door's one primary action lands. /pal is budgeted; the surface it opens was not.
The Social tab, one of the five phone destinations.
Social Posts, and the heaviest of the shared social shells.
Discovery, on the same shell, budgeted apart so a change to one cannot hide inside the other.
The drink lanes surface, same shell again.

ceilingRaises.why: This path is not a surface any more. app/drinks/page.tsx has been a permanentRedirect to /social?tab=discover since #765 (6 August), so the row measures the discover tab plus one redirect round trip, and /discover is budgeted 1000 for exactly that content and passes at 688. The 400 here was written for the drink lanes page that no longer exists. Measured on the Avrea runner at 684 ms (samples 708/684/488), and locally against a production build under the tracked throttle at 856 ms against /social's 692 ms on the same run, the two carrying identical decoded JS. The captain ruled the raise on 6 September 2026. It goes to /discover's own figure and no further, so the redirect can never cost more than the page it lands on.

routes.why: Private threads. It carries the photo pipeline, so it is the social surface most able to grow.
The per-viewer notification feed.

The signed-in account hub, and the document /profile actually serves. #1411 painted its copy from the HTML and its LCP fell to about 770 ms, comfortably inside this ceiling, but it also mounted the whole Wanted panel across the identity-loading paint and took the route to 1375 KB over 71 requests against ceilings of 1290 and 66. The ceilings were left where they are rather than moved to fit the measurement, which is the whole rule of this file, and the route came back under them instead: the head of the panel stays in the HTML and the body, the account hub, the crews panel and the timeline load after paint, for 1199 KB over 59 requests at 612 ms.
Arrival for a brand new account, and the one route where a slow paint is the first thing anybody sees.

The city question, on the path to every non-London night. Its gate is the chooser's own LIST rather than its <main>: #1402 moved every launch route onto the Screen primitive and this route lost its own class in the swap, so main.screen would prove a Screen mounted rather than that the chooser did.
The Moment capture surface.
The Round diary, where a night's spend is recorded. It is the one social surface that writes money figures, so it is budgeted rather than assumed light.
The crawl index, a crawlable family.
The borough index above the crawlable price family, so the family's own entrance is measured.
The historic pubs index.
The live Pint Index: the page every trust claim and every citation points at.
The founding members wall.
The contributor leaderboard.
The we-are-out feed, on the shared feed shell. Budgeted apart from /feed so a change to one cannot hide inside the other.
A legal page composes nothing per request, so it and /terms are the floor every server-rendered route here is judged against.
The other half of that floor. Two pages on one shell: if they ever disagree, something composed.
The Places tab, which sets the one city Map, Out and Near follow. It shipped in #1368 after this sweep's route list was drawn, and an unbudgeted route is one nothing can regress.
